name: phone-input
title: Phone Input
description: A phone number input with country detection, international formatting and a searchable country picker.

<script lang="ts" module>
	import { cn, type WithElementRef } from '$UTILS$.js';
	import type { FormEventHandler, HTMLInputAttributes } from 'svelte/elements';

	/** A DOM event whose `currentTarget` is known to be the phone `<input>`. */
	export type PhoneInputFieldEvent = Event & { currentTarget: EventTarget & HTMLInputElement };

	export type PhoneInputFieldProps = WithElementRef<
		Omit<HTMLInputAttributes, 'value' | 'type' | 'readonly' | 'files'>,
		HTMLInputElement
	> & {
		/**
		 * Whether the field is disabled. OR-ed with the root's own `disabled`.
		 *
		 * @default false
		 */
		disabled?: boolean;
		/**
		 * Whether the field is read-only. OR-ed with the root's own `readOnly`.
		 *
		 * @default false
		 */
		readOnly?: boolean;
		/**
		 * Whether the field is required. OR-ed with the root's own `required`.
		 *
		 * @default false
		 */
		required?: boolean;
		/**
		 * Called before the field normalises the typed text — upstream's `onChange`. Calling
		 * `preventDefault()` discards the edit and snaps the displayed value back.
		 */
		oninput?: FormEventHandler<HTMLInputElement> | null;
	};
</script>

<script lang="ts">
	import { Input } from '$lib/components/ui/input/index.js';

	import { getPhoneInputContext } from './phone-input.svelte.js';

	let {
		ref = $bindable(null),
		disabled = false,
		readOnly = false,
		required = false,
		oninput: oninputProp,
		class: className,
		...restProps
	}: PhoneInputFieldProps = $props();

	const root = getPhoneInputContext('<PhoneInput.Field>');

	const isDisabled = $derived(disabled || root.disabled);
	const isReadOnly = $derived(readOnly || root.readOnly);
	const isRequired = $derived(required || root.required);

	/**
	 * Bumped by every edit. React re-renders a controlled input and snaps the DOM back after every
	 * keystroke, including one that produces an identical formatted string (typing `a` into
	 * `+1 408`); Svelte only patches the attribute when the derived value actually *changes*, so
	 * without a generation counter a rejected character would linger in the DOM (research R-09).
	 */
	let syncGeneration = $state(0);

	const pendingSync = $derived([syncGeneration, root.displayValue] as const);

	// DOM-only: this effect writes `element.value` and never any reactive state, which is why it is
	// an effect and not a `$derived`. No caret arithmetic — upstream performs none either.
	$effect(() => {
		const [, next] = pendingSync;
		const element = ref;
		if (element && element.value !== next) element.value = next;
	});

	$effect(() => {
		root.fieldElement = ref;
		return () => {
			root.fieldElement = null;
		};
	});

	function handleInput(event: PhoneInputFieldEvent) {
		syncGeneration++;

		if (isDisabled || isReadOnly) return;

		oninputProp?.(event);
		if (event.defaultPrevented) return;

		root.setValueFromInput(event.currentTarget.value);
	}
</script>

<!--
	The owned attributes are emitted *before* `restProps` (so a caller can override them) and the
	class, placeholder, value and handler *after* it (so a caller cannot), reproducing upstream's JSX
	order exactly (research R-12). `value` is one-way — never `bind:value`, which would make a second
	writer fight the snap-back above.
-->
<Input
	bind:ref
	type="tel"
	inputmode="tel"
	aria-required={isRequired}
	aria-invalid={root.invalid}
	data-slot="phone-input-field"
	disabled={isDisabled}
	readonly={isReadOnly}
	required={isRequired}
	{...restProps}
	class={cn(
		'h-full flex-1 rounded-s-none rounded-e-lg border-0 bg-transparent shadow-none ring-0 focus-visible:ring-0 disabled:bg-transparent aria-invalid:ring-0 dark:bg-transparent dark:disabled:bg-transparent',
		className
	)}
	placeholder={root.placeholder}
	value={root.displayValue}
	oninput={handleInput}
/>

import { getUnmaskedValue } from '$lib/components/ui/mask-input/index.js';

/**
 * One selectable entry of the country dropdown. Identical to upstream's `Country` interface

 */

	/** ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. */
	code: string;
	/** Country name. */
	name: string;
	/** Country calling code (e.g., `"+1"` for US). */

	/** Optional flag emoji. */
	flag?: string;

/** The root's placeholder when the caller supplies none (upstream `phone-input.tsx:473`). */
export const DEFAULT_PHONE_PLACEHOLDER = 'Enter phone number';

/**
 * The display name of a region, falling back to the code itself when the platform cannot resolve
 * it. `locale` is not exposed as a prop — upstream hard-codes the default too.
 */
export function getCountryName(countryCode: string, locale = 'en'): string {
	try {
		const regionNames = new Intl.DisplayNames([locale], { type: 'region' });
		return regionNames.of(countryCode) ?? countryCode;
	} catch {
		return countryCode;
	}
}

/** The regional-indicator pair for a country code, e.g. `"US"` becomes the US flag emoji. */
export function getFlagEmoji(countryCode: string): string {
	const codePoints = countryCode
		.toUpperCase()
		.split('')
		.map((char) => 127397 + char.charCodeAt(0));
	return String.fromCodePoint(...codePoints);
}

/**
 * The 239 built-in countries, sorted by display name.
 *
 * Memoised: upstream re-derives the list on every render (a React default-argument evaluation),
 * which produces byte-identical output but repeats 239 `Intl.DisplayNames` lookups. The cached
 * array is the value every root defaults to, so it must never be mutated — every consumer that
 * sorts (see {@link detectCountryFromNumber}) works on a copy.
 */
let countriesCache: Country[] | undefined;

export function getCountries(): Country[] {
	countriesCache ??= COUNTRY_DATA.map(([iso2, dialCode]): Country => {
		const code = iso2.toUpperCase();
		return {
			code,
			name: getCountryName(code),
			dialCode: `+${dialCode}`,
			flag: getFlagEmoji(code)
		};
	}).sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name));

	return countriesCache;
}

/** Every digit of a string, the one step this engine shares with `mask-input` (research R-02). */
function digitsOf(value: string): string {
	return getUnmaskedValue({ value });
}

/**
 * The country a canonical value belongs to, or `undefined` when nothing matches.
 *
 * Longest dial code first, so `+1242` beats `+1`; when the best match is `+1` — shared by more than
 * twenty countries — the US entry wins. A shared non-`+1` dial code has no tie-break, so the first
 * entry in the caller's list order wins (the sort is stable).
 */
export function detectCountryFromNumber(value: string, countries: Country[]): Country | undefined {
	if (!value?.startsWith('+')) return undefined;

	const digits = digitsOf(value.slice(1));
	if (!digits) return undefined;

	const sorted = [...countries].sort((a, b) => b.dialCode.length - a.dialCode.length);

	const matches: Country[] = [];
	for (const country of sorted) {
		if (digits.startsWith(country.dialCode.slice(1))) {
			matches.push(country);
		}
	}

	if (matches.length === 0) return undefined;

	if (matches.length > 1 && matches[0]?.dialCode === '+1') {
		const usCountry = matches.find((country) => country.code === 'US');
		if (usCountry) return usCountry;
	}

	return matches[0];
}

/**
 * The display string for a canonical value: the detected dial code, then the remaining digits in
 * groups of three. Deliberately not a national format — upstream ships no per-country grouping.
 */
export function formatPhoneNumber(value: string, countries: Country[]): string {
	if (!value) return '';

	const normalized = value.startsWith('+') ? value : `+${value}`;

	const digits = digitsOf(normalized.slice(1));
	if (!digits) return '+';

	const detected = detectCountryFromNumber(`+${digits}`, countries);
	const dialCodeLength = detected ? detected.dialCode.slice(1).length : Math.min(digits.length, 3);

	const countryCode = digits.slice(0, dialCodeLength);
	const rest = digits.slice(dialCodeLength);

	let formatted = `+${countryCode}`;

	if (rest) {
		formatted += ' ';
		for (let i = 0; i < rest.length; i++) {
			if (i > 0 && i % 3 === 0) {
				formatted += ' ';
			}
			formatted += rest[i];
		}
	}

	return formatted;
}

/**
 * Turn what the user typed into the canonical value, plus whether they led with a `+` — the flag
 * that decides when auto-detection may run (research R-06). Upstream `phone-input.tsx:769-775`.
 */
export function normalizePhoneInput(raw: string): { value: string; startsWithPlus: boolean } {
	const startsWithPlus = raw.startsWith('+');
	const digits = digitsOf(raw);

	return {
		value: digits ? `+${digits}` : startsWithPlus ? '+' : '',
		startsWithPlus
	};
}
